title: fix(cli)!: the CLI opens a sign-in page only for an http(s) address and never through a shell, and os mcp connect registers only an address that passes one parse
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the published skill's `os mcp connect` row and its eval state no exit condition, no Windows lookup, no address character set and no output rule, so nothing they teach changes; `skills/**` is outside this order's file surface

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:命令行登录只为 http 或 https、且字符规范的登录地址自动打开浏览器;连接 Claude Code 时,只登记并打印通过同一套地址校验的服务地址,地址里带用户名或密码会被拒绝;服务器返回的名字、报错、登录地址和验证码一律以单行可见字符打印;在 Windows 上若找到的是 npm 安装的批处理包装,命令以退出码 1 停下并打印那一行。
- 为什么做:命令行工具启动外部程序一律不经过系统外壳、只交出校验过的地址,打印服务器文字时不让它改动终端显示,属于安全加固,由安全席位派发,维护者已裁定采用"停下并打印"方案并保留自定义地址的路径限制。
- 出错会怎样:最坏是浏览器没有自动打开、某个地址被拒绝登记、某段服务器文字显示成转义形式,或 Windows 上没有自动登记,用户照屏幕提示手动完成即可;整单可直接撤回。
- 要你做什么:无

## What changes

The rules:

- **The CLI opens a sign-in page only for an http(s) address written in plain URL characters, and never through a shell.** `os login` and `os cloud login` hand the parsed address to the platform's opener as one argv element with `shell: false` (`open` on macOS, `xdg-open` elsewhere, `rundll32.exe url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` by its absolute path on Windows). An address outside the rule is printed, not opened, with a line saying so. "Browser opened automatically" is printed only when the opener was started; an opener that could not be started prints its own line.
- **Server text prints as one line of printable characters.** Every string a server supplies that `os mcp connect`, `os login` or `os cloud login` prints or throws (an environment's name and id, an error text, the sign-in address, the user code, the account's email and id) goes through one sanitiser, `utils/terminal-text.ts`: control characters (C0 with CR, LF and TAB, DEL, C1), the Unicode line and paragraph separators and the bidirectional controls are shown as visible escapes, and the length is capped. The browser still opens the parsed address unchanged. `--json` records are unchanged.
- **After the Endpoint, Name and Connect block, `os mcp connect` prints nothing from the control plane but the block's own name and address.** The Sign-in and Revoke lines now name "the environment" instead of its display name.
- **`os mcp connect` registers and prints only an address that passes one parse, on both paths.** Whether it comes from `--url` or from the control plane, the address parses as an http(s) URL with no user name or password, is rebuilt from the parsed origin, holds no control character, and holds only letters, digits, `-._~:/`, `[` and `]` (an IPv6 host's brackets, and in a `--url` path prefix). An address from the control plane must also be a bare host (an optional scheme and port). Anything else exits 1, with nothing registered and no Connect line printed; each refusal names the characters accepted and a way on (the console for an environment; `claude mcp add` by hand for `--url`). The printed Connect line double-quotes an address holding a bracket, since sh-family shells read brackets as a pattern; the registered argv is unquoted. The `--url` path-prefix restriction stays, by the maintainer's word.
- **`os mcp connect` starts `claude` from an argv array with `shell: false` on every platform.** On Windows it runs the `.exe`/`.com` that the first matching fully qualified `PATH` entry holds (rooted at a drive letter, or a UNC share), by its absolute path; the current directory, relative entries and entries rooted at the current drive are not searched. A batch-file shim there is not run (ruled option A): exit 1, the printed `claude mcp add` line, and both remedies.
- **Every program the CLI starts carries no shell beyond four measured allowances**, each pinned by its statement and its inputs (Acceptance notes).

**BREAKING (Windows): a batch-file `claude` is no longer run.**

- FROM: on a Windows install whose `claude` is a batch-file shim (`claude.cmd`, which an npm global install writes), `os mcp connect` registered the server and exited 0.
- TO: it registers nothing and exits 1, printing the `claude mcp add` line and saying why.
- The fix: run the printed `claude mcp add …` line yourself, or install Claude Code's native Windows build and run `os mcp connect` again.

**BREAKING: `os mcp connect` registers and prints only an address that passes the rule above.**

- FROM: an address outside it was registered and printed as given; a user name or password in `--url` was dropped without a word.
- TO: it is refused with exit 1; nothing is registered and no Connect line is printed. Each refusal names the characters accepted and a way on.
- The fix: for `--url`, pass a base URL in those characters with no user name or password, or run `claude mcp add --transport http NAME URL` yourself with the server's MCP address; for an environment, check its address in the ObjectOS Cloud console.

ADR-0087 disposition (stated in the changeset's marker): not-required, `no-migration-prescription` — no schema key, accepted value, export or stored row moves; there is nothing for a migration to rewrite and no tombstone.

Changeset: `@objectstack/cli` patch, carrying the `!` summary, both declaration lines, the marker and both BREAKING blocks. The CLI reference (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, `os login`, `os cloud login`, `os mcp connect`) states the same rules.

## Tests

Every case title states its rule or a number; sample inputs live in the data, never in a name.

- `packages/cli/test/server-text-reaches-the-terminal-as-one-line.test.ts` (new):
  - `terminalText`, 5 cases: every C0, DEL and C1 code point, the separators and the bidirectional controls come out as visible escapes; an escape sequence loses its introducer; printable text, other scripts and emoji are unchanged and a second pass changes nothing; the cap counts its ellipsis.
  - A TypeScript-AST source pin over the six files those flows print from. Every argument of a print site (the `print*` helpers, `console.*`, `process.stdout|stderr.write`, `this.log|warn|error`), every `new Error(…)` message and every `message:` property must be made of literals, `terminalText(…)`, a declared text function whose own returns are held to the same rule, a `const` so made, or one of four declared line-safe expressions (the validated name and address, the line built from them, and the install-target refusal whose `message:` templates the pin also holds). Findings must be empty; every flow file has print sites and the total holds a floor of 100 (111 measured); a roster entry nothing uses reds. Detector battery: 19 loud cases (a floor per sink kind) and 14 quiet ones. The walk reads six files: the file ran in 93 ms.
- `packages/cli/test/mcp-connect.test.ts` — on the registering and the `--print` path, a display name holding control characters leaves the Endpoint, Name and Connect lines byte-identical to a plain run, adds no line, leaves exactly one line starting `Connect`, and nothing after the block names the environment; environment ids, names and the control plane's error text in a refusal each stay on their line; the bracket quoting; the `--url` user name and password refusal on both paths; the way on in both refusals; the control-plane address refusals, numbered 1 to 16; an address with `_` and `~` registers.
- `packages/cli/test/sign-in-page-opens-http-only-without-a-shell.test.ts` — both device flows: the printed sign-in address and user code carry no control byte and add no line, and the browser opens the parsed address unchanged; the server's error text reaches the thrown error as one line; the refused-address cases, numbered; a UNC share entry is searched, both spellings.
- `packages/cli/test/cli-launches-without-a-shell.pin.test.ts` — the shell-program rule reads either side of `||`, `??` and `?:`; a `createRequire(…)` result, held or called inline, counts as `require`. Battery now 40 loud cases (11 / 11 / 8 / 10 per rule, each held to that floor) and 20 quiet. The header lists what the pin still cannot see. Measured: the file ran in under 1 s, its walk inside `beforeAll`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Allow-listed in the source pin, measured, not changed here.** The rule names three text classes an allowed command line may carry: text the CLI wrote; text held to a fixed character set or a closed set of values; the invoking user's own argument to the same command. `commands/doctor.ts` `probeTool` (CLI-written constant probes; every caller passes a literal, pinned); `commands/dev.ts` `pnpm [--filter PACKAGE --fail-if-no-match] dev` (the invoking user's own argument, chosen over a character set because pnpm owns the filter grammar); `commands/init.ts` `PM install` (closed set); `utils/skills-catalog.ts` `npm pack` on Windows (exact-version charset and a quoted CLI-created directory).
- `describeEnvironment` is shared, so `os deploy`'s and `os package publish --install`'s environment lines print the control plane's name and id as one line too.
- Not measured on a Windows host: the opener's argv and the client lookup are pinned with a mocked file probe and a mocked runner. A `PATH` entry that is a link rather than a regular file is not measured.
- The `--url` narrowing also refuses a base URL whose path prefix holds a percent-encoded or punctuation character; such a server has no spelling under the rule, and the refusal names registering it with `claude mcp add` by hand.

## Verification

<details><summary>Reverse verification (fix committed first; each mutation through an anchor that must hit, the named files run, the restore proven blob == HEAD and an empty git diff HEAD)</summary>

19 mutation runs, 16 distinct ablations, each red and then restored:

- One-line rule: the environment name unsanitised in the shared describer: 3 red. The user code unsanitised (cloud flow): 2 red (behaviour and source pin). The sign-in address unsanitised (`os login`): 2 red. The server's error text unsanitised in the thrown error: 2 red. An account email unsanitised (`os cloud login`): 1 red (source pin). The sanitiser disabled: 10 red.
- Source-pin detector: text-function returns unchecked: 2 red.
- Address rule: bracket quoting removed: 2 red. `--url` user name and password refusal removed: 2 red. The control-plane refusal's way on removed: 16 red. The `--url` refusal's way on removed: 1 red.
- Windows lookup: UNC entries not searched: 1 red.
- No-shell pin: a shell program behind `||`/`??` unread, in `?:` unread, an inline `createRequire` load unread, a held `createRequire` result unread: 1 red each.
- Three first attempts were refused by the mutation tool before any test ran (each replacement already occurred in the file); each was re-run with a disjoint replacement.
- After all of them: 0 changed paths, empty `git diff HEAD`.

</details>

<details><summary>Local runs (final head bde1e1b17 unless a line names another)</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (tsc + `check:test-typecheck`) → `VERDICT command-exit 0`, `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- The four files above → `Test Files 4 passed (4)` (mcp-connect 42, sign-in 41, the new pin 10, the no-shell pin 5).
- CLI `unit` tier (`vitest run --project unit`) → `Test Files 442 passed (442) · Tests 6316 passed (6316)`. The `integration` tier is declared to CI.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the ten touched TypeScript files → exit 0; `check-nul-bytes` → OK; control-byte scan over every touched file → no match; `check-platform-checklist --changed-from origin/main` → exit 0.
- Derived gate list (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`), 102 families, each exit captured before any pipe: 102 × exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: `102 derived, 102 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. The derivation warned that the tree is 7 commits behind `origin/main`; `main` was not merged, as no conflict or main-caused red asks for it.
- Dogfood battery (the title carries `!`): `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/dogfood^...' build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the lock → `VERDICT command-exit 0` · `Test Files 487 passed | 3 skipped (490)` · `Tests 4125 passed | 68 skipped (4193)`, no failure.
- Not measured: a Windows host.

</details>

Read first: `packages/cli/src/utils/terminal-text.ts`, `packages/cli/test/server-text-reaches-the-terminal-as-one-line.test.ts` (the sinks and the roster), `packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/connect.ts` (`run`, `mcpUrlFromBase`, `claudeMcpAddLine`).

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/server-text-reaches-the-terminal-as-one-line.test.ts test/mcp-connect.test.ts test/sign-in-page-opens-http-only-without-a-shell.test.ts test/cli-launches-without-a-shell.pin.test.ts` → `Test Files 4 passed (4) · Tests 98 passed (98)`.
